summary: Pyrometrics is an interactive, open-access web platform that centralizes, translates, and operationalizes NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) data on microgravity combustion.   To address the Fire in Free Fall challenge, we developed a unified workspace featuring four core modules: an AI-powered Specific Questions assistant grounded directly in PSI research; a structured Research catalog with dynamic filters and interactive hyperlink trees; an automated Comparison engine that maps variables, similarities, and differences across studies; and an open-source Interactive Flammability Prevention Model linked to GitHub, allowing researchers to fork, modify, and submit peer-reviewed fire simulations via pull requests.   Because fire in microgravity spreads unpredictably and poses severe risks—as seen in the 1997 Mir station incident—making PSI data actionable is critical for designing safer materials, optimizing fire suppression systems, and protecting crews on future Artemis lunar missions and deep-space habitats
details:
The Problem & Why It Matters In the absence of Earth's gravity, flames behave unpredictably, spreading rapidly and resisting conventional suppression methods. Historical emergencies—such as the severe 1997 fire aboard the Mir space station that blocked evacuation routes and filled modules with toxic smoke—highlight the critical danger of combustion in enclosed spacecraft. As humanity prepares for sustained lunar exploration under NASA's Artemis program, understanding microgravity fire dynamics is essential to engineer fire-resistant materials, refine suppression protocols, and safeguard astronaut lives. However, valuable scientific findings from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository currently remain fragmented and difficult to cross-reference.

Our Solution: Pyrometrics Pyrometrics is a segmented, intuitive web platform designed for undergraduate/graduate students, educators, and aerospace engineers. It bridges the gap between raw PSI datasets and practical fire-safety engineering through four integrated modules:

  1. Specific Questions (Grounded AI Assistant): A specialized artificial intelligence connected to a cloud repository of NASA PSI documentation. Users can ask complex, open-ended questions regarding flame behavior in microgravity and receive accurate, traceable answers backed directly by official scientific literature.
  2. Interactive Research Catalog: A searchable, filterable database organizing PSI combustion experiments by study type, fuel, test conditions, objective, and terrestrial benefits. Selecting any study reveals full metadata, author bios, methodologies, problem-solution breakdowns, and an interactive hyperlink tree that maps guiding scientific questions directly to their corresponding data points.
  3. Cross-Study Comparison Engine: Users can select multiple PSI investigations to automatically analyze connections between variables, experimental environments, and outcomes. The system generates a comparative synthesis alongside visual outlines and dot-circle diagrams highlighting overlapping findings and key divergences.
  4. Interactive Flammability Prevention Model (GitHub-Integrated): A dynamic simulation sandbox where users manipulate environmental and material variables to test fire prevention scenarios. Connected directly to a GitHub repository, the module enables decentralized scientific collaboration: researchers can create independent branches, log parameter adjustments via commits for 100% reproducibility, and submit validated improvements via pull requests to be merged into the main platform.

Differentiation, Feasibility & Sustainability

  • Key Differentiator: Unlike static repositories, Pyrometrics unifies data querying, multi-study synthesis, and collaborative simulation in a single environment.
  • Technical Feasibility: Built on an agile, low-cost architecture leveraging open-source tools (GitHub, Vercel, Supabase) and verified public datasets from NASA’s PSI database.
  • Scalability & Freemium Model: Core catalog access, filters, and basic AI queries remain permanently free to democratize space science. Advanced computational simulations and multi-study visual mapping operate under an accessible Freemium tier, complemented by an open-science donation system and institutional partnerships. In the future, the architecture is ready to integrate repositories from international space agencies and IEEE standards.
